title: Etale extension by zero commutes with base change for module sheaves
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $j:V\to X$ be etale, and form the fibre-product square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $V'=Y\times_XV$, $j':V'\to Y$, and $f':V'\to V$. For a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda_V$-modules on $V_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the base-change morphism $\beta_M:j'_!((f')^{-1}M)\to f^{-1}(j_!M)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], where inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] on sheaves of modules [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and $j_!$, $j'_!$ are etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y$-modules. Hence $\beta^{-1}$ is an isomorphism $f^{-1}(j_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!((f')^{-1}M)$, natural in $M$. This is Stacks Project Lemma 59.70.5, Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), in the module-sheaf form.

proof.text: *The two adjunctions and $\beta$.* $j'$ is etale, as a base change of the etale $j$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. On sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules we have $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] and $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3). Composing [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], $L_1=f^{-1}j_!$ is left adjoint to $R_1=j^{-1}f_*$ and $L_2=j'_!f'^{-1}$ is left adjoint to $R_2=f'_*j'^{-1}$, as functors between $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ (Stacks: "$j'_!f'^{-1}$ is left adjoint to $f'_*(j')^{-1}$ and $f^{-1}j_!$ is left adjoint to $j^{-1}f_*$"). By [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], $\beta:L_2\to L_1$ is the natural transformation whose conjugate with respect to these two adjunctions is the underived exchange transformation $\Ex^0_\square:R_1\to R_2$ of the cartesian square $\square=(f,f',j,j',\mathrm{id})$, top $j'$, bottom $j$.

source.place: Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), line 11493, proof lines 11506-11514, first sentence

proof.text: *The right adjoints agree on abelian sheaves.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction](2) with the following dictionary. Its $f:X\to Y$ is our $f:Y\to X$, and its etale $j:V\to Y$ is our $j:V\to X$. Its $X_V=X\times_YV$ is our $V'=Y\times_XV$ with $j_X=j'$ and $f_V=f'$, and its square $\square_j$, with the identity as identification, is our $\square$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. It gives the following. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $Y_{\Et}$, the underived exchange morphism $\Ex^0_{\square,F}:j^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*j'^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves on $V_{\Et}$. On sections it is the identification $F(W\times_XY)=F(W\times_VV')$, for $W\to V$ etale. This is Stacks' "$f'_*(j')^{-1}=j^{-1}f_*$ because $f_*$ commutes with etale localization (by construction)".

source.place: Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), line 11493, proof lines 11506-11514, second sentence

proof.text: *The right adjoints agree on sheaves of modules.* Let $G\in\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear], $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ (formed on the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$) is a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_V$-modules $R_1G\to R_2G$. By step 2 it is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves, so each component $\Ex^0_{\square,G}(W)$ is a bijective $\Lambda_V(W)$-linear map. Its inverse is then $\Lambda_V(W)$-linear, and these inverses commute with the restriction maps because the $\Ex^0_{\square,G}(W)$ do. So the inverse is a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_V$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ is an isomorphism in $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Hence $\Ex^0_\square:R_1\to R_2$ is a natural isomorphism of functors $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$; it is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear].

source.place: Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), line 11493, proof lines 11506-11514, "on abelian sheaves and on sheaves of modules" (statement); the module form is written out here

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], a natural transformation $\tau:L_2\to L_1$ is an isomorphism if and only if its conjugate $\tau^c:R_1\to R_2$ is. By step 1, $\beta^c=\Ex^0_\square$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], and by step 3 this is a natural isomorphism. Hence $\beta:j'_!f'^{-1}\to f^{-1}j_!$ is a natural isomorphism. So for every $M\in\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $\beta_M:j'_!((f')^{-1}M)\to f^{-1}(j_!M)$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y$-modules, and the inverses $\beta_M^{-1}$ are natural in $M$. This is Stacks' conclusion "$j'_!f'^{-1}=f^{-1}j_!$": two functors whose right adjoints are isomorphic are themselves isomorphic.

split_report.summary: The canonical base-change morphism of the statement was defined in no node. It is now defined in the new node def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map as the conjugate, for the composite adjunctions f^{-1}j_! -| j^{-1}f_* and j'_!f'^{-1} -| f'_*j'^{-1}, of the underived exchange Ex^0: j^{-1}f_* -> f'_*j'^{-1}. With that definition it runs j'_!f'^{-1}M -> f^{-1}j_!M. This is the direction a conjugate of the exchange has without first inverting it, and the direction of the slopmaster2 open-immersion analogue. The statement is corrected to this direction, cites the new definition, and states the inverse iso f^{-1}j_!M -> j'_!f'^{-1}M explicitly, which is what the only citer (lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible) uses. The proof follows Stacks 03S6 exactly: compare the right adjoints. The abelian isomorphism of the right adjoints is the closed node lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction (unit sk-thm-reduction, a tool since it is closed). Its Lambda-linearity is the new node lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear. The conclusion uses the Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate. The adjunction j_! -| j^{-1} is taken from lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives (unit sk-thm-iff, on route); f^{-1} -| f_* on modules is taken from prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (sk-def-exchange, on route). Stalk descriptions (03S5) and the free-module case lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-free-etale-module are not needed.
